summary: Control-plane heartbeat TCP sessions dropped by stateful corporate firewall session timeout causing repeated agent reconnections
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports agents in their private deployment repeatedly dropping and reconnecting to Redwood control-plane. Impact: several model-serving hosts flapped offline briefly, causing request routing to fallback and increased tail latency for production customers. Observation window: 2026-02-27 22:30 - 2026-02-28 03:00 UTC.

Impact: Intermittent agent disconnects across a subset of customer-managed subnets resulted in degraded capacity for their Dedicated pools. No model artifact fetch failures observed; control-plane GRPC stream resets were primary symptom.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peered to Redwood control-plane over TGW). Control-plane uses long-lived gRPC streams from agent to control-plane (keepalive interval 60s). Customer reports corporate perimeter firewall with stateful TCP session idle timeout of 90s and deep-packet inspection in place.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Deploy a new agent on customer's subnet behind corporate perimeter firewall.
2) Allow agent to establish control-plane gRPC stream to Redwood control-plane.
3) Let agent sit idle (no requests) for >2 minutes.
4) Observe agent reconnects; control-plane shows a short-lived STREAM_CLOSE and new CONNECT event.

Observed behavior: Agents disconnect after ~90-120s of idleness. Control-plane logs show TCP RST / EOF on the server-side and immediate reconnects from the agent. Customer's firewall logs show the NAT session closed for the outbound control-plane connection due to idle timeout. Reconnects cause ephemeral port churn and temporary token re-auth attempts leading to transient 429s on the customer side.

Expected behavior: Long-lived control-plane gRPC streams remain established for the configured agent keepalive window (default SDK keepalive 60s) and do not get torn down by network middleboxes.

Logs / evidence:
- Control-plane endpoint logs (redacted): "stream closed: EOF after 1m45s idle" (timestamps matching customer reports).
- Agent logs (customer provided): "WARN: control-plane connection dropped: read tcp: connection reset by peer" followed by "INFO: reconnecting in 2s".
- Customer firewall/NAT logs: entries showing session removed after 90s of idle, NAT translation table freed.
- wireshark trace (customer supplied) shows FIN from firewall to server and no TCP FIN from agent.

Temporary workaround used: Customer increased agent keepalive ping interval to 30s (via agent config) to keep the session busy enough to avoid idle NAT expiry. This reduced flapping while we investigated.

Root cause hypothesis: The corporate stateful firewall/NAT has a conservative idle session timeout (~90s) that closes idle TCP sessions. Long-lived gRPC streams that are idle (no data/pings at OS/TCP level for >90s) are silently terminated by the middlebox. The agent's application-level keepalives were insufficient to produce network activity at the frequency required to keep the NAT entry alive.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 2026-02-28 00:10 UTC - Support received packet captures and firewall policy excerpts. 2026-02-28 01:00 UTC - Reproduced idle tear down in lab by emulating firewall with 90s timeout. 2026-02-28 02:15 UTC - Confirmed control-plane sees EOF/RST matching customer's firewall NAT clear.

Hypotheses tested:
- MTU or fragmentation issues: ruled out (no PMTUD errors, artifact downloads unaffected).
- TLS inspection/SNI stripping: ruled out (TLS handshake completes, certificates validated).
- Agent bug causing FIN: ruled out (lab agent maintained connection without middlebox).

Evidence points to external session lifetime enforcement at customer's perimeter. Customer policies show an outbound session table TTL set to 90s for "idle TCP".

Consequence: Reconnects caused ephemeral port rotation leading to short windows of token requeue and occasional 429 throttling on subsequent requests. Also increased control-plane connection churn visible in metrics.
actions_taken:
1) Advised customer to temporarily set agent keepalive interval to 30s (applied and validated). 2) Provided configuration snippet for persistent HTTP ping on control-channel to maintain NAT binding for customers unable to change perimeter device settings. 3) Opened INT-442 with Network Reliability team to evaluate server-side keepalive strategy and graceful reconnect backoff changes. 4) Created internal runbook entry and Confluence page for 'Agent keepalive vs stateful firewall' guidance.

Config snippet shared with customer:
- agent.config: { "control_keepalive_interval_s": 30, "reconnect_backoff_ms": 2000 } (note: redacted as single-line here; full example provided in Confluence)

Customer-side remediation: Customer updated firewall policy to extend idle TCP timeout for Redwood control-plane CIDRs to 900s where possible. This was coordinated with their network security team and applied to affected perimeter boxes on 2026-03-01 18:40 UTC.
resolution:
Root cause: Perimeter stateful firewall/NAT idle timeout closed control-plane TCP sessions when streams were idle. Resolution: Dual approach — customer extended firewall idle timeout for Redwood control-plane IP ranges; Redwood documented a recommended agent keepalive configuration and server-side conservative keepalive adjustments were scheduled. Result: No agent flapping observed after changes.

Follow-ups:
- Engineering to land PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/agent-proxy/pull/432 to make a default optional low-overhead keepalive for private deployments. (ETA Q2 2026).
- Support to add knowledge base article and include keepalive tuning in private deployment checklist.
- Customer to monitor for any residual 429s and report back if seen.

Ticket closed after customer validation on 2026-03-02.
